full_judgment:
4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Pirganj by his judgment and decree dated 30-4-2005 decreed the suit on the findings, inter-alia, that the predecessor of the defendants during his life time delivered back possession of the suit land to the predecessor of the plaintiffs on receipt of the money paid for the mortgage and the successors of the mortgagors have been enjoying and possessing the suit land; once a mortgage always a mortgage and limitation for filing a suit for redemption of mortgage being 60 years, the suit having been filed within 51 years, the same was not barred by limitation and the plaintiffs were entitled to redeem the mortgage; the suit having been filed under rule 1 of Order XXXIV of the Code of Civil Procedure, section 95 A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act) cannot be a bar for redemption of the mortgaged property even if the transaction in question became past and closed. 

 "V. For that the High Court Division erred in law and facts by holding on the principle of 'once a mortgage always a mortgage', that the respondents are entitled to the redemption for getting back the suit land by setting aside the finding of the Appellate Court that the transaction under a sale deed of 1947 with a condition to re-convey if payment is made within 5 years being a usufructuary mortgage it became a past and closed transaction in terms of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 inasmuch as the period of 7 years was over long before, 1972.
